trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Consultant: Sales (FAIS)
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: To provide needs-based financial advice, sales, and service to individual retail banking customers, enabling them to meet their personal financial goals while ensuring compliance with FAIS, Treating Customers Fairly (TCF), and bank risk frameworks.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Proactively acquire customers and deliver sales against agreed targets.
  - Deliver efficient and professional customer service and resolve queries across all touchpoints.
  - Support lead generation and simplex activities to contribute to branch growth.
  - Action and conversion of quality leads and campaigns; maintain pipeline hygiene and accurate reporting.
  - Execute DHA and MVNO offerings precisely and securely, meeting service levels and audit requirements.
  - Champion digital and self-service adoption including customer education to reduce assisted transactions.
  - Operate flexibly across diverse branch formats and customer segments.
  - Deliver first‑time‑right customer outcomes and uphold service excellence.
  - Apply governance, risk and compliance standards (incl. FAIS, AML/CFT, TCF, POPIA) in every interaction.
  - Collaborate within the team and contribute to a continuous improvement of performance culture.
  - Deliver a consistently exceptional in-branch customer experience by proactively welcoming, guiding, and supporting customers, while promoting efficient service, alternative banking channels, and upholding Absa’s service standards, image, and brand in a safe, professional, and well‑managed branch environment.
  - Conduct comprehensive personal financial needs analyses
  - Provide advice and sell approved retail banking products (transactional accounts, savings, lending, credit, insurance, investments as applicable)
  - Explain product features, benefits, risks, and costs clearly
  - Achieve individual sales, growth, and cross-sell targets
  - Build and maintain long-term relationships with assigned customers
  - Proactively manage customer portfolios to retain and grow value
  - Conduct regular portfolio reviews and engagement follow-ups
  - Deliver a professional, consistent, and personalised customer experience through welcoming, guiding, and supporting customers, while promoting efficient service, alternative banking channels
  - Uphold Absa’s service standards, image, and brand in a safe, professional, and well‑managed branch environment.
  - Resolve customer queries and manage escalations effectively
  - Support digital adoption and financial education initiatives
  - Operate in accordance with FAIS, FICA, AML, and internal risk policies
  - Maintain accurate advice records, documentation, and disclosures
  - Complete regulatory training and CPD requirements
  - Identify and escalate conduct or operational risks
Must-have requirements:
  - Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Banking
  - Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Finance
Location: Carnarvon
Work mode: onsite
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Consultant: Sales (FAIS)

Absa Group

Carnarvon · onsite

About us
Empowering Africa's tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.

About the role
You will give needs-based financial advice, sell and service retail banking products to individual customers in our Carnarvon branch. You help customers meet their personal financial goals while working within FAIS, Treating Customers Fairly (TCF) and the bank's risk frameworks.

What you'll do
• Conduct comprehensive personal financial needs analyses with individual retail banking customers
• Advise on and sell approved retail banking products, including transactional accounts, savings, lending, credit, insurance and investments as applicable
• Explain product features, benefits, risks and costs clearly so customers can make informed choices
• Achieve your individual sales, growth and cross-sell targets
• Acquire new customers proactively and convert quality leads and campaigns, keeping your pipeline and reporting accurate
• Build long-term relationships with assigned customers, review portfolios regularly and follow up on engagements to retain and grow value
• Resolve customer queries across all touchpoints and manage escalations, aiming for first-time-right outcomes
• Execute DHA and MVNO offerings precisely and securely, meeting service levels and audit requirements
• Promote digital and self-service channels and educate customers, reducing assisted transactions
• Welcome, guide and support customers in branch, upholding Absa's service standards, image and brand in a safe, professional and well-managed environment
• Apply governance, risk and compliance standards in every interaction, including FAIS, FICA, AML/CFT, TCF and POPIA
• Maintain accurate advice records, documentation and disclosures
• Complete regulatory training and CPD requirements
• Identify and escalate conduct or operational risks
• Work flexibly across different branch formats and customer segments, and contribute to team performance and continuous improvement

What you need
• Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Banking, or Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Finance
• Ability to conduct financial needs analyses and advise on retail banking products
• Working knowledge of FAIS, FICA, AML and TCF requirements, needed because every customer interaction must meet these standards
• Clear communication skills to explain product features, benefits, risks and costs to customers

Nice to have
• Experience generating leads and converting campaigns in a branch environment
• Experience supporting customers to adopt digital and self-service banking channels

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
